Shows your phone screen on the car display, so you can watch any app. Apps that block screen recording (Netflix, Prime Video and similar) show a black picture. Keep the phone unlocked and turn it sideways for a full-screen picture.
Touch control is on: taps on the car screen control the phone.
Touch control is off. Without it, the mirrored screen can only be watched, not tapped.
Find “AutoCarPlay touch control” under Installed apps / Downloaded apps and turn it on.

Plug an ELM327 OBD-II adapter (Bluetooth or Wi-Fi) into the car\'s diagnostic port, under the dashboard near the steering wheel. For Bluetooth, pair it in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings first (the PIN is usually 1234 or 0000). Then open “Car dashboard” on the car screen to see engine speed, temperatures, battery voltage and fault codes while parked.

1. Update Android Auto from the Play Store. Your phone needs Android 15 or newer (see the note above).
2. Open Android Auto settings (button below, or phone Settings → Connected devices → Connection preferences → Android Auto).
3. Scroll to the bottom and tap “Version” 10 times, then allow developer settings.
4. Tap ⋮ (top right) → Developer settings → turn on “Unknown sources”.
5. Go back → Customize launcher → make sure AutoCarPlay is ticked.
6. Unplug and reconnect the phone to the car (or restart the car screen), then open AutoCarPlay from the Android Auto launcher while parked.

Android shows AutoCarPlay as a game, because games are the only full-screen apps Android Auto allows when an app is not from the Play Store.

Touch control on Android 13+: if Android says the setting is restricted, open phone Settings → Apps → AutoCarPlay → ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings”, then turn it on again.
